references.text: The same offerings were given by Nahshon, son of Amminadab, from the tribe of Judah—a silver plate, a silver bowl, and fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering. This shows the repeated pattern of identical gifts from each tribal leader.
Nethanel, son of Zuar, from the tribe of Issachar, gave the same offerings—a silver plate weighing 130 shekels, a silver bowl weighing 70 shekels, and fine flour mixed with oil.
Eliab, son of Helon, from the tribe of Zebulun, brought identical offerings with the same weight and contents.
Elisur, son of Shedeur, from the tribe of Reuben, gave the same type of offerings at the dedication of the tabernacle.
The sanctuary shekel is mentioned as the standard unit of weight, the same scale used to weigh the silver objects in this verse.
The grain offering (mincha) of fine flour mixed with oil is described here, the same type of offering mentioned in Numbers 7:37.
Fine flour mixed with oil as part of the sacrificial system at the dedication, parallel to the grain offering mentioned here.
